children.text: yasmād anyo na paro 'sti jāto ya ābabhūva bhuvanāni viśvā
children.translated_text: He than whom no other higher one has been born, who brought forth all the worlds.

children.text: jyotiṣmān asya ṣoḍaśī bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: His <s>Ṣoḍaśī</s> becomes luminous, who knows thus.

children.text: ekaviṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai pratitiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stoma</s> is the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s>, for establishment; he becomes established.

children.text: Chapter 13
govit pavasva vasuviddhiraṇyavid iti pañcamasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
children.translated_text: The opening verse of the fifth day is, 'Flow, finder of cows, finder of wealth, finder of gold.'

children.text: govid vā etad vasuviddhiraṇyavidyacchakvaryaḥ
children.translated_text: These <s>Śakvarī</s> verses are indeed finder of cows, finder of wealth, finder of gold.

children.text: paśavaś śakvaryaḥ sarvaṃ paśubhir vindate
children.translated_text: The <s>Śakvarī</s> verses are cattle; he obtains everything through cattle.

children.text: tvaṃ suvīro asi somaviśvavid ityeṣa yāva suvīro yasya paśavas tad eva tad abhivadati
children.translated_text: In 'You are rich in heroes, O <s>Soma</s>, finder of all,' that very thing is declared: he whose cattle are abundant is truly rich in heroes.

children.text: tās te kṣarantu madhumad ghṛtaṃ paya iti madhumad vai ghṛtaṃ payaḥ paśavaḥ kṣaranti tad eva tad abhivadati
children.translated_text: In 'May those of yours flow with honey-sweet ghee and milk,' ghee and milk are indeed honey-sweet; cattle flow. That very thing it declares.

children.text: pavamānasya viśvavid ity anurūpo bhavati
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>Pavamāna</s>, finder of all' is the <s>anurūpa</s> (corresponding verse).

children.text: viśvam eva tadvit tam abhivadati viśvaṃ hi paśubhir vindate
children.translated_text: By this it calls him finder of all; for he obtains everything through cattle.

children.text: pra te sargā asṛkṣata iti sṛṣṭānīva hyetarhyahāni
children.translated_text: 'Your outpourings have been released' is used, for at this point the days are, as it were, released.

children.text: pūrvam u caiva tad rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati yat pūrvaṃ rūpeṇānuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avaruddhyai
children.translated_text: Thus he repeats the earlier form with the later form. Because he repeats the earlier with its form, that is the correspondingness of the <s>anurūpa</s>; a son corresponding to him is born to the one who knows thus. The <s>stotrīya</s> and <s>anurūpa</s> are two <s>tṛca</s>s, for securing the in-breaths and out-breaths.

children.text: saptarcau bhavataḥ chandasāṃ dhṛtyai
children.translated_text: The two are seven-versed, for the firmness of the metres.

children.text: caturṛco bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: It is four-versed, for establishment.

children.text: tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
children.translated_text: The last is a <s>tṛca</s>; by the very breath with which they go forth, they rise up toward it.

children.text: triṇava eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai puṣṭyai trivṛd vā eṣa puṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stoma</s> is the <s>Triṇava</s>, for establishment and nourishment; this nourished one is indeed threefold.

children.text: tava śriyo varṣasy eva vidyuta ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgneya Ājya</s> is, 'Your splendors are like the lightning of the rain-cloud.'

children.text: śrīr vai paśavaḥ śrīḥ śakvaryaḥ tad eva tad abhivadati
children.translated_text: Cattle are splendor; the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses are splendor. That very thing it declares.

children.text: agneś cikitra uṣasām ivetaya itītānīva hyetarhyahānīti
children.translated_text: In 'Agni's brilliance has appeared, like the coming of dawns,' at this point the days are, as it were, already gone.

children.text: ā te yatente rathyo yathā pṛthag ity eva hyetarhyahāni yatante
children.translated_text: In 'They strive toward you, like chariot-horses separately,' at this point the days do indeed strive separately.

children.text: purūruṇā ciddhy asty avo nūnaṃ vāṃ varuṇa iti maitrāvaruṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> is, 'For even with abundant help there is protection; now there is protection for you two, O <s>Varuṇa</s>.'

children.text: yad vai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ tad varuṇo gṛhṇāti tad eva tad avayajati
children.translated_text: Whatever in the sacrifice is badly offered, <s>Varuṇa</s> seizes; that very thing he thereby expiates by sacrifice.

children.text: uttiṣṭhann ojasā saha ity aindram
children.translated_text: The <s>Aindra</s> is, 'Rising up together with strength.'

children.text: pañca vā ṛtava utthānasya rūpam ojasā sahety ojasaiva vīryeṇa sahottiṣṭhanti
children.translated_text: There are five seasons, the form of rising up; by 'together with strength' they rise up with strength and vigor itself.

children.text: indrāgnī yuvām ima iti rāthantaram aindrāgnam
children.translated_text: The <s>Rāthantara Aindrāgna</s> is, '<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, you two, these.'

children.text: rathantaram etat parokṣaṃ yacchakvaryo rāthantaram eva tad rūpaṃ nirdyotayati stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This, namely the <s>Śakvarī</s> verses, is the <s>Rathantara</s> in indirect form; he thereby makes the <s>Rāthantara</s> form shine forth. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: arṣā soma dyumattama iti viṣṇumatyo gāyatryo bhavanti
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses containing <s>Viṣṇu</s> are used, beginning 'Flow, O <s>Soma</s>, most brilliant.'

children.text: brahma vai gāyatrī yajño viṣṇur brahmaṇy eva tad yajñaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>brahman</s> (sacred formulation); <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the sacrifice. Thereby he establishes the sacrifice in <s>brahman</s> itself.

children.text: soma uṣvāṇas sotṛbhir iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivaitās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
children.translated_text: The verse 'O <s>Soma</s>, roaring with the pressers' is the form of the <s>Simā</s> verses; by their own form he perfects them.

children.text: yat soma citram ukthyam iti gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses beginning 'Whatever wondrous, laudable thing, O <s>Soma</s>' are truly <s>Triṣṭubh</s> in form; therefore they are performed in the place of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>s.

children.text: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatra</s> is used; whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> explanation of the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies.

children.text: yaṇvaṃ bhavati paśavo vai yaṇvaṃ paśūnām avaruddhyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Yaṇva</s> is used; cattle are the <s>Yaṇva</s>, for securing cattle.

children.text: santataṃ gāyati yajñasya saṃtatyai
children.translated_text: He sings continuously, for the continuity of the sacrifice.

children.text: adhyardheḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
children.translated_text: It is the <s>Adhyardheḍa</s>; for such is the form of this day.

children.text: śākalaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Śākala</s> is used.

children.text: etena vai śakalaḥ pañcame 'hani pratyatiṣṭhat pratitiṣṭhati śākalena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: With this <s>Śakala</s> became established on the fifth day; the one praising with the <s>Śākala</s> becomes established.

children.text: vārśaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Vārśa</s> is used.

children.text: vṛśo vaijānas tryaruṇasya traidhātavasyaikṣvākasya purohita āsīt sa aikṣvāko 'dhāvayat brāhmaṇakumāraṃ rathena vyachinat sa purohitam abravīt tava mā purodhāyām idam īdṛg upāgād iti tam etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vārśaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛśa Vaijāna</s> was the <s>purohita</s> (domestic priest) of <s>Tryaruṇa Traidhātava</s>, an <s>Aikṣvāka</s>. That <s>Aikṣvāka</s> drove on and cut down a brahmin boy with his chariot. He said to his <s>purohita</s>, 'Under your priesthood such a thing has befallen me.' He made that boy rise again with this <s>sāman</s>. That indeed was what he desired then. The <s>Vārśa</s> is a desire-winning <s>sāman</s>; by it he secures desire itself.

children.text: adhyardheḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
children.translated_text: It is the <s>Adhyardheḍa</s>; for such is the form of this day.

children.text: mānavaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Mānava</s> is used.

children.text: etena vai manuḥ prajāpatiṃ bhūmānam agacchat prajāyate bahur bhavati mānavena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: By this, indeed, <s>Manu</s> reached the abundance that is <s>Prajāpati</s>. The one who praises with the <s>Mānava</s> procreates and becomes numerous.

children.text: ānūpaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Ānūpa</s> is used.

children.text: etena vai vadhryaśva ānūpaḥ paśūnāṃ bhūmānam āśnuta paśūnāṃ bhūmānam aśnuta ānūpena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: By this, indeed, <s>Vadhryaśva Ānūpa</s> attained an abundance of cattle. The one who praises with the <s>Ānūpa</s> attains an abundance of cattle.

children.text: vāmraṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Vāmra</s> is used.

children.text: māmārṣeyeṇa praśastaṃ yaṃ vai gām aśvaṃ puruṣaṃ praśaṃsanti vāma iti taṃ praśaṃsanty ahar evaitena praśaṃsanti
children.translated_text: It is praised with the <s>Māmārṣeya</s>. Whichever cow, horse, or man people praise, they praise that one as 'lovely'; with this they praise the day itself.

children.text: adhyardheḍaṃ tathā hy etasyāhno rūpam
children.translated_text: It is the <s>Adhyardheḍa</s>, for such is the form of this day.

children.text: triṇidhanam āgneyaṃ bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: An <s>Āgneya</s> with three <s>nidhana</s>s is used, for stability.

children.text: agniḥ sṛṣṭo nodadīpyata taṃ prajāpatir etena sāmnopādhamat sa udadīpyata dīptiś ca vā etat sāma brahmavarcasaṃ ca dīptiś caivaitena brahmavarcasaṃ cāvarundhe
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s>, when created, did not blaze up. <s>Prajāpati</s> blew upon him with this <s>sāman</s>, and he blazed up. This <s>sāman</s> is both radiance and <s>brahmavarcasa</s> (sacred brilliance); by it one secures radiance and <s>brahmavarcasa</s>.

children.text: śaiśavaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Śaiśava</s> is used.

children.text: śiśur vā āṅgiraso mantrakṛtāṃ mantrakṛd āsīt sa pitṝn putrakā ity āmantrayata taṃ pitaro 'bruvan na dharmaṃ karoṣi yo naḥ pitṝn sataḥ putrakā ity āmantrayama iti so 'bravīd ahaṃ vāva vaḥ pitāsmi yo mantrakṛd asmīti taṃ deveṣv apṛcchanta te devā abruvann eṣa vāva pitā yo mantrakṛd iti tad vai sa udajayad ujjayati śaiśavena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śiśu Āṅgirasa</s> was a maker of mantras among the makers of mantras. He addressed the fathers as 'little sons.' The fathers said to him, 'You are not acting according to <s>dharma</s>, since you address us, who are fathers, as little sons.' He said, 'I indeed am your father, for I am a maker of mantras.' They questioned the gods about him, and the gods said, 'He indeed is the father who is the maker of mantras.' That, truly, he won; the one who praises with the <s>Śaiśava</s> wins.

children.text: gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
children.translated_text: They chant on <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, for stability and for <s>brahmavarcasa</s>. By the very breath with which they set out, they rise up to it.

children.text: viṣṇumatyo gāyatryo bhavanti tad u traiṣṭubhād rūpān na yanti stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses contain <s>Viṣṇu</s>; thus they do not depart from the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> form. The <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: indraḥ prajāpatim upādhāvad vṛtraṃ hanānīti tasmā etacchandobhya indriyaṃ vīryaṃ nirmāya prāyacchad etena śaknuhīti tacchakvarīṇāṃ śakvarītvaṃ sīmānam abhinat tat simā mahnyām akarot tan mahnyā mahān ghoṣa āsīt tan mahānāmnyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> ran to <s>Prajāpati</s>, saying, 'May I slay <s>Vṛtra</s>.' From these metres he fashioned might and heroic power and gave it to him, saying, 'By this you will be able.' That is the <s>Śakvarī</s>-nature of the <s>Śakvarī</s>s. He broke through the boundary; he made that boundary great. From that greatness there was a great sound; hence the <s>Mahānāmnī</s>s.

children.text: diśaḥ pañcapadā dādhārartūn ṣaṭpadā chandāṃsi saptapadā puruṣaṃ
children.translated_text: With the five-footed one he supported the directions; with the six-footed one, the seasons; with the seven-footed one, the metres and the person.

children.text: dvyopaśāḥ saṃstutā bhavanti tasmād dvyopaśāḥ paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: They are praised as having two <s>upaśa</s>s; therefore animals have two <s>upaśa</s>s.

children.text: iḍe abhito 'thakāraṃ tasmācchṛṅge tīkṣṇīyasī stūpāt
children.translated_text: They place the 'atha' syllable on both sides of the <s>iḍā</s>; therefore the horns are sharper than the hump.

children.text: upakṣudrā gāyati tasmād upakṣudrāḥ paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: He sings in a slightly diminished way; therefore animals are somewhat small.

children.text: asaṃśliṣṭā gāyati tasmād asaṃśliṣṭāḥ paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: He sings without joining; therefore animals are unjoined from one another.

children.text: nānārūpā gāyati tasmān nānārūpāḥ paśavaḥ
children.translated_text: He sings in varied forms; therefore animals are of varied forms.

children.text: āpo vai kṣīrarasā āsaṃste devāḥ pāpavasīyasād abibhayur yad apa upanidhāya stuvate pāpavasīyaso vidhṛtyai
children.translated_text: The waters, indeed, had the sap of milk. The gods feared what was worse than evil. When they chant after placing water nearby, it is for warding off what is worse than evil.

children.text: vidhṛtiḥ pāpavasīyaso bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: There is a warding off of what is worse than evil for the one who knows thus.

children.text: gāyatram ayanaṃ bhavati brahmavarcasakāmasya svarṇidhanaṃ madhunāmuṣmiṃlloka upatiṣṭhate traiṣṭubham ayanaṃ bhavaty ojaskāmasyāthakāraṇidhanam ājyenāmuṣmiṃlloka upatiṣṭhate jāgatam ayanaṃ bhavati paśukāmasyeḍānidhanaṃ payasāmuṣmiṃlloka upatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatra</s> course is used for one who desires <s>brahmavarcasa</s>; its <s>nidhana</s> is 'svar,' and in yonder world he attends with honey. The <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> course is used for one who desires vigor; its <s>nidhana</s> is the 'atha' syllable, and in yonder world he attends with ghee. The <s>Jāgata</s> course is used for one who desires cattle; its <s>nidhana</s> is the <s>iḍā</s>, and in yonder world he attends with milk.

children.text: añjasāryo mālyaḥ śakvarīḥ prārautsīd iti hovācālammaṃ pārijānataṃ rajanaḥ kauṇeyo yady enāḥ pratiṣṭhāpaṃ śakṣyatīty etad vā etāsām añjayati pratiṣṭhitā ya ābhiḥ kṣipraṃ prastutya kṣipram udgāyati
children.translated_text: '<s>Añjasārya Mālya</s> has damaged the <s>Śakvarī</s>s,' so <s>Rajana Kauṇeya</s> said to <s>Ālamma Pārijānata</s>, 'if he will be able to set them firm.' This indeed straightens them. They are firmly established when one quickly sets them forth and quickly sings out with them.

children.text: śakvarībhiḥ stutvā purīṣeṇa stuvate
children.translated_text: Having praised with the <s>Śakvarī</s>s, they praise with the <s>Purīṣa</s>.

children.text: paśavo vai śakvaryo gauṣṭhaḥ purīṣaṃ goṣṭham eva tat paśubhyaḥ paryasyanti tam evainān pravartayantyavisraṃsāya
children.translated_text: The <s>Śakvarī</s>s are cattle, and the <s>Purīṣa</s> is the cow-stall. Thus they set the cow-stall around the cattle; they set them moving within it, so that they do not slip away.

children.text: indro madāya vāvṛdha ity avardhanta hy etarhi
children.translated_text: '<s>Indra</s> grew for exhilaration' is used, for at this point they indeed grew.

children.text: tāsu bārhadgiram
children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Bārhadgira</s> is used.

children.text: svādor itthā viṣuvata iti viṣuvān vai pañcamam ahas tāsu rāyovājīyam
children.translated_text: 'From the sweet one, thus, at the <s>Viṣuvat</s>' is used, for the fifth day is indeed the <s>Viṣuvat</s>. Among these, the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> is used.

children.text: indro yatīn sālāvṛkebhyaḥ prāyacchat teṣāṃ traya udaśiṣyanta pṛthuraśmir bṛhadgirī rāyovājas te 'bruvan ko na imān putrān bhariṣyatīty aham itīndro 'bravīt tān ādhinidhāya paricāryaṃ carad vardhayaṃs tān vardhayitvābravīt kumārakā varān vṛṇīdhvam iti kṣatraṃ mahyam ity abravīt pṛthuraśmis tasmā etena pārthuraśmena kṣatraṃ prāyacchat kṣatrakāma etena stuvīta kṣatrasyaivāsya prakāśo bhavati brahmavarcasaṃ mahyam ity abravīt bṛhadgiris tasmā etena bārhadgireṇa prāyacchat brahmavarcasakāma etena stuvīta brahmavarcasī bhavati paśūn mahyam ity abravīd rāyovājas tasmā etena rāyovājīyena paśūn prāyacchat paśukāma etena stuvīta paśumān bhavati
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> handed the <s>Yati</s>s over to the <s>Sālāvṛka</s>s. Three of them survived: <s>Pṛthuraśmi</s>, <s>Bṛhadgiri</s>, and <s>Rāyovāja</s>. They said, 'Who will nourish these sons for us?' 'I will,' said <s>Indra</s>. Taking them under his care, he tended them while making them grow. When he had made them grow, he said, 'Little boys, choose boons.' 'Royal power for me,' said <s>Pṛthuraśmi</s>. To him he gave royal power with this <s>Pārthuraśma</s>; one who desires royal power should praise with it, and royal power becomes manifest for him. 'Sacred brilliance for me,' said <s>Bṛhadgiri</s>. To him he gave it with this <s>Bārhadgira</s>; one who desires <s>brahmavarcasa</s> should praise with it, and he becomes possessed of <s>brahmavarcasa</s>. 'Cattle for me,' said <s>Rāyovāja</s>. To him he gave cattle with this <s>Rāyovājīya</s>; one who desires cattle should praise with it, and he becomes possessed of cattle.

children.text: pārthuraśmaṃ rājanyāya brahmasāma kuryāt bārhadgiraṃ brāhmaṇāya rāyovājīyaṃ vaiśyāya svenaivaināṃstadrūpeṇa samardhayati stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should make the <s>Pārthuraśma</s> the <s>brahmasāman</s> for a <s>Rājanya</s>, the <s>Bārhadgira</s> for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and the <s>Rāyovājīya</s> for a <s>Vaiśya</s>. With their own corresponding form he makes them prosper. The <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: asāvy aṃśur madāya iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verse 'The soma-stalk has been pressed for exhilaration' is used. The third pressing is indeed full of exhilaration and sap; thereby he places exhilaration and sap in it.

children.text: abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhadyaśa ity abhīti rathantarasya rūpaṃ bṛhad iti bṛhata ubhayos saha rūpam upaityubhau hi varṇāvetad ahaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Toward splendor, great in fame' is used. The word 'abhi' is the form of the <s>Rathantara</s>; 'bṛhat' is the form of the <s>Bṛhat</s>. He obtains the form of both together, for this day has both forms.

children.text: prāṇā śiśur mahīnām iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ mahyo hi simāḥ svenaivainās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
children.translated_text: The line "prāṇā śiśur mahīnām" is the form of the <s>Sīmā</s> chants; for the <s>Sīmā</s> chants are great. By that very form of theirs he makes them prosper.

children.text: pavasva vājasātaya iti vaiṣṇavyo 'nuṣṭubho bhavanti
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses beginning "pavasva vājasātaya" are used.

children.text: yajño vai viṣṇur yad atra nāpi kriyate tad viṣṇunā yajñenāpi karoti
children.translated_text: The sacrifice is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Whatever is not performed here, he nevertheless performs by means of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by means of the sacrifice.

children.text: indur vājī pavate gonyoghā iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivainās tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
children.translated_text: The line "indur vājī pavate gonyoghā" is the form of the <s>Sīmā</s> chants; by that very form of theirs he makes them prosper.

children.text: triṣṭubhaḥ satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmājjagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
children.translated_text: They are really <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses, but <s>Jagatī</s> in form; therefore they are performed in the place of the <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatra</s> is used; whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> explanation of the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies here.

children.text: santani bhavati pañcamasyāhnas santatyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Santani</s> is used, for the continuity of the fifth day.

children.text: vāg vā eṣā pratatā yad dvādaśāhas tasyā eṣa viṣuvān yat pañcamam ahas tām evaitena saṃtanoti
children.translated_text: This extended speech is the twelve-day rite. Its <s>viṣuvant</s> (central point) is the fifth day; by this he extends that very speech continuously.

children.text: cyāvanaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Cyāvana</s> is used.

children.text: prajātir vai cyāvanaṃ prajāyate bahur bhavati cyāvanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Cyāvana</s> is procreation. One who praises with the <s>Cyāvana</s> is propagated and becomes numerous.

children.text: ebhyo vai lokebhyo vṛṣṭir apākrāmat tāṃ prajāpatiś cyāvanenācyāvayad yad acyāvayat taccyāvanasya cyāvanatvaṃ cyāvayati vṛṣṭiṃ cyāvanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: Rain had departed from these worlds. <s>Prajāpati</s> set it in motion with the <s>Cyāvana</s>; because he made it move, that is the <s>Cyāvana</s>'s character as <s>Cyāvana</s>. One who praises with the <s>Cyāvana</s> sets rain in motion.

children.text: krośa bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Krośa</s> is used.

children.text: etena vā indra indrakrośe viśvāmitrajamadagnī imā gāva ityākrośat paśūnām avaruddhyai krośaṃ kriyate
children.translated_text: With this, in <s>Indra</s>'s cry, <s>Indra</s> called out to <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>, "These cows!" The <s>Krośa</s> is performed for the securing of cattle.

children.text: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaurīvita</s> is used; whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> explanation of the <s>Gaurīvita</s> applies here.

children.text: ṛṣabhaḥ śākvaro bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛṣabha Śākvara</s> is used.

children.text: paśavo vai śakvaryaḥ paśuṣveva tan mithunam apy arjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
children.translated_text: The <s>Śakvarī</s> verses are cattle. Thereby he supplies a mating pair among the cattle, for procreation; cattle without a bull do not reproduce.

children.text: pārthaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Pārtha</s> is used.

children.text: etena vai pṛthur vainya ubhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam āśnutobhayeṣāṃ paśūnām ādhipatyam aśnute pārthena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: With this <s>Pṛthu Vainya</s> attained lordship over both kinds of cattle. One who praises with the <s>Pārtha</s> attains lordship over both kinds of cattle.

children.text: aṣṭeḍaḥ padastobho bhavati
children.translated_text: The eight-<s>eḍa</s> <s>Padastobha</s> is used.

children.text: indro vṛtrāya vajram udayacchat taṃ ṣoḍaśabhir bhogaiḥ paryabhujat sa etaṃ padastobham apaśyat tenāpāveṣṭayad apāveṣṭayann iva gāyet pāpmano 'pahatyai
children.translated_text: When <s>Indra</s> lifted the thunderbolt against <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Vṛtra</s> enclosed him in sixteen coils. He saw this <s>Padastobha</s>, and with it he unwound himself. He should sing as if unwinding, for the removal of evil.

children.text: pāpmā vāva sa tam agṛhṇāt taṃ padastobhenāpāhatāpa pāpmānaṃ hate padastobhena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: It was evil indeed that had seized him. He struck it away with the <s>Padastobha</s>; one who praises with the <s>Padastobha</s> strikes evil away.

children.text: pador uttamam apaśyat tat padastobhasya padastobhatvam
children.translated_text: He saw the last part of the <s>pada</s> (metrical foot); that is the <s>Padastobha</s>'s character as <s>Padastobha</s>.

children.text: dvādaśanidhano bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: The twelve-<s>nidhana</s> form is used, for establishment.

children.text: dāśaspatyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Dāśaspatya</s> is used.

children.text: yāṃ vai gāṃ praśaṃsanti dāśaspatyeti tāṃ praśaṃsanty ahar evaitena praśaṃsanti
children.translated_text: When they praise a cow as <s>Dāśaspatya</s>, they praise that very cow; by this they praise the day itself.

children.text: nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pavamāna</s> chants have <s>nidhana</s> endings, for the stability of the day. The <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: ā te agna idhīmahi iti
children.translated_text: The verse beginning "ā te agna idhīmahi" is used.

children.text: apacchid iva vā etad yajñakāṇḍaṃ yad ukthāni yad eti salomatvāyaiva
children.translated_text: For this section of the sacrifice, namely the <s>uktha</s> chants, is as if cut off when it proceeds; this is simply for giving it continuity.

children.text: indrāya sāma gāyata iti pūrṇāḥ kakubhas tenānaśanāyuko bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Kakubh</s> verses beginning "indrāya sāma gāyata" are full; by that he becomes one whose life is not one of hunger.

children.text: puruṣo vai kakup puruṣam eva tan madhyataḥ prīṇāti
children.translated_text: The <s>Kakubh</s> is the person; thereby he gratifies the person in the middle.

children.text: asāvi soma indra ta iti simānāṃ rūpaṃ svenaivaināṃs tad rūpeṇa samardhayati
children.translated_text: The line "asāvi soma indra ta" is the form of the <s>Sīmā</s> chants; by that very form of theirs he makes them prosper.

children.text: saṃjayaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Saṃjaya</s> is used.

children.text: devāś ca vā asurāśca samadadhata yatare naḥ saṃjayāṃsteṣāṃ naḥ paśavo 'sān iti te devā asurān saṃjayena samajayan yat samajayaṃs tasmāt saṃjayaṃ paśūnām avaruddhyai saṃjayaṃ kriyate
children.translated_text: The gods and the <s>Asuras</s> made an agreement: "Whichever of us shall conquer, to them shall our cattle belong." The gods conquered the <s>Asuras</s> with the <s>Saṃjaya</s>. Because they conquered, it is called <s>Saṃjaya</s>. The <s>Saṃjaya</s> is performed for the securing of cattle.

children.text: saumitraṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Saumitra</s> is used.

children.text: dīrghajihvī vā idaṃ rakṣo yajñahā yajñiyān avalihaty acarat tām indraḥ kayācana māyayā hantuṃ nāśaṃsatātha ha sumitraḥ kutsaḥ kalyāṇa āsa tam abravīd imām acchā brūṣveti tām acchā brūta sainam abravīn nāhaitan na śuśruva priyam iva tu me hṛdayasyeti tām ajñapayat tāṃ saṃskṛte 'hatāṃ tad vāva tau tarhy akāmayetāṃ kāmasani sāma saumitraṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
children.translated_text: <s>Dīrghajihvī</s>, a demoness who destroyed the sacrifice, went about licking up the sacrificial things. <s>Indra</s> could not hope to kill her by any stratagem. Now <s>Sumitra Kutsa</s> was handsome. He said to him, "Address this woman." He addressed her, and she said to him, "No, I have not failed to hear this; but it is as if dear to my heart." He made an appointment with her, and they struck her down at the prepared place. Then those two indeed desired one another. The <s>Saumitra</s> is a desire-winning <s>sāman</s>; by this he secures desire.

children.text: sumitraḥ san krūram akar ity enaṃ vāg abhyavadat taṃ śug ārchat sa tapo 'tapyata sa etat saumitram apaśyat tena śucam apāhatāpaśucaṃ hate saumitreṇa tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: Speech reproached him, saying, "Being <s>Sumitra</s>, you did a cruel thing." Grief came upon him. He practiced austerity, and he saw this <s>Saumitra</s>. With it he struck grief away; one who praises with the <s>Saumitra</s> strikes grief away.

children.text: mahāvaiśvāmitraṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Mahāvaiśvāmitra</s> is used.

children.text: pāpmānaṃ hatvā yad amahīyanta tan mahāvaiśvāmitrasya mahāvaiśvāmitratvam
children.translated_text: Because, after striking down evil, they became great, that is the <s>Mahāvaiśvāmitra</s>'s character as <s>Mahāvaiśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: hāyā ihayā ohā oheti paśūn evaitena nyauhanta
children.translated_text: With the sounds "hāyā, ihayā, ohā, ohe" they thereby drive in the cattle.

children.text: trīḍaṃ bhavati trirātrasya dhṛtyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Trīḍa</s> is used, for the stability of the three-night rite.

children.text: dravantīm iḍām uttamām upayanti ṣaṣṭhasyāhnaḥ santatyai
children.translated_text: They come to the final <s>Dravantī Iḍā</s>, for the continuity of the sixth day.

children.text: triṇava eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai puṣṭyai trivṛd vā eṣa puṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stoma</s> is just the <s>Triṇava</s>, for establishment and fullness; for this is a strengthened <s>Trivṛt</s>.

children.text: jyotir yajñasya pavate madhupriyam iti ṣaṣṭhasyāhnaḥ pratipad bhavati
children.translated_text: "jyotir yajñasya pavate madhupriyam" is the opening verse of the sixth day.

children.text: jyotir vai gāyatrī chandamāṃ jyotiḥ revatī sāmnāṃ jyotis trayastriṃśaḥ stomānāṃ jyotir eva tat samyak saṃdadhāsy api ha putrasya putro jyotiṣmān bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> is light among the meters; the <s>Revatī</s> is light among the <s>sāman</s> chants; the thirty-threefold is light among the <s>stomas</s>. Thus he will fit together light itself correctly; even his son's son becomes radiant.

children.text: madhu priyam iti paśavo vai revatyo madhupriyaṃ tad eva tad abhivadati
children.translated_text: With "madhu priyam": the <s>Revatī</s> verses are cattle, and it states of them precisely that they are honey-dear.

children.text: madintamo matsara indriyo rasa itīndriyaṃ vai vīryaṃ rasaḥ paśavas tad eva tad abhivadati
children.translated_text: With "madintamo matsara indriyo rasa": power, vigor, sap, and cattle are what it states precisely.

children.text: amṛkṣata pra vājina ity anurūpo bhavati
children.translated_text: "amṛkṣata pra vājina" is the corresponding verse.

children.text: sṛṣṭānīva hy etarhy ahāni
children.translated_text: For at this point the days are as if released.

children.text: pūrvam u caiva tad rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati yat pūrvaṃ rūpam apareṇa rūpeṇānuvadati tad anurūpasyānurūpatvam anurūpa enaṃ putro jāyate ya evaṃ veda stotrīyānurūpau tṛcau bhavataḥ prāṇāpānānām avaruddhyai
children.translated_text: And he then recites that earlier form with a later form. Because he recites the earlier form with a later form, that is the correspondingness of the <s>Anurūpa</s>. A son corresponding to him is born to the one who knows thus. The <s>Stotrīya</s> and <s>Anurūpa</s> are two triplets, for securing the in-breaths and out-breaths.

children.text: daśarcau bhavato daśākṣarā virāṭ vairājam annam annādyasyāvaruddhyai
children.translated_text: They are ten-verse units. The <s>Virāj</s> has ten syllables; food is <s>Virāj</s>, for securing food and the eating of food.

children.text: uttaro daśarco bhavati sodarka indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya
children.translated_text: The later one is a ten-verse unit, with a continuation, so that the faculty, vigor, and essence do not flow away.

children.text: yatra ve devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
children.translated_text: Where the gods saw faculty, vigor, and essence, there they pressed after it.

children.text: caturṛco bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: It is a four-verse unit, for stability.

children.text: dhvasre vai puruṣantī tarantapurumīḍhābhyāṃ vaitadaśvibhyāṃ sahasrāṇy aditsatāṃ tāv aikṣetāṃ kathaṃ nāv idam āttam apratigṛhītaṃ syād iti tau praty etāṃ dhvasrayoḥ puruṣantyor ā sahasrāṇi dadmahe tarat sa mandī dhāvatīti tato vai tat tayor āttam apratigṛhītam abhavat
children.translated_text: <s>Dhvasrā</s> and <s>Puruṣantī</s> wished to give thousands to <s>Taranta</s> and <s>Purumīḍha</s>, the two <s>Vaitadaśvi</s>s. Those two considered, 'How could this possession of ours be taken, yet not received?' In reply to <s>Dhvasrā</s> and <s>Puruṣantī</s> they gave this: 'We give thousands to <s>Dhvasrā</s> and <s>Puruṣantī</s>; let that exhilarated one run across.' From that, what belonged to those two became taken but not received.

children.text: āttam asyāpratigṛhītaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: What belongs to the one who knows thus becomes taken but not received.

children.text: vinārāśaṃso bhavaty ubhayasyānnādyasyāvaruddhyai mānuṣasya ca daivasya ca
children.translated_text: The <s>Vinārāśaṃsa</s> is used, for securing both kinds of food and food-eating, the human and the divine.

children.text: tṛca uttamo bhavati yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
children.translated_text: The last is a triplet. With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up to it.

children.text: trayastriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai devatāsu vā eṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>stoma</s> is thirty-threefold, for stability; for this is established among the deities.

children.text: imaṃ stomam arhate jātavedasa ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgneya</s> <s>ājya</s> is 'This <s>stoma</s> is worthy of <s>Jātavedas</s>.' It has a continuation, so that the faculty, vigor, and essence do not flow away. Where the gods saw faculty, vigor, and essence, there they pressed after it.

children.text: prativāṃ sūra udita iti sūravan maitrāvaruṇam
children.translated_text: 'The sun has risen toward you two' is the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s>, containing <s>sūra</s>.

children.text: anto vai sūro 'nta etat ṣaṣṭham ahar ahnām anta eva tad ante stuvate pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: The sun is the end, and this sixth day is the end of the days. Thus they praise at the very end, at the end, for stability.

children.text: bhinddhi viśvā apadviṣa ity aindraṃ sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan
children.translated_text: 'Break apart all hostile powers' is the <s>Aindra</s>. It has a continuation, so that the faculty, vigor, and essence do not flow away. Where the gods saw faculty, vigor, and essence, there they pressed after it.

children.text: yajñasya hi stha ṛtvija ity aindrāgnaṃ sodarkam indriyasya vīryasya rasasyānatikṣārāya yatra vai devā indriyaṃ vīryaṃ rasam apaśyaṃs tad anunyatudan stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'For you two are the priests of the sacrifice' is the <s>Aindrāgna</s>. It has a continuation, so that the faculty, vigor, and essence do not flow away. Where the gods saw faculty, vigor, and essence, there they pressed after it. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: indrāyendo marutvata iti marutvatyo gāyatryo bhavanti
children.translated_text: 'For <s>Indra</s>, O drop, accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>' is used; the <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses are <s>Marutvatī</s>.

children.text: marutvaddhi mādhyandinaṃ savanam
children.translated_text: For the midday pressing is accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>.

children.text: mṛjyamānaḥ suhastya iti simānāṃ rūpam
children.translated_text: 'Being cleansed by one of good hands' is the form of the <s>Simā</s> verses.

children.text: samānaṃ vai simānāṃ rūpaṃ revatīnāṃ ca simābhyo hy adhirevatyaḥ prajāyante
children.translated_text: The form of the <s>Simā</s> verses and of the <s>Revatī</s> verses is the same, for the <s>Adhirevatī</s> verses are born from the <s>Simā</s> verses.

children.text: etam u tyaṃ daśa kṣipa ity ādityā ādityā vā imāḥ prajās tāsām eva madhyataḥ pratitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: 'That one there, with ten fingers' is used as the <s>Āditya</s> verses. These creatures are the <s>Ādityas</s>; he thereby stands firm in their very midst.

children.text: gāyatryaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
children.translated_text: Although they are <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, they have the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses; therefore they are performed in the place of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>s.

children.text: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatra</s> is used; whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> explanation of the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies.

children.text: iṣovṛdhīyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Iṣovṛdhīya</s> is used.

children.text: paśavo vā iṣovṛdhīyaṃ paśūnām avaruddhyā iṣe vai pañcamam ahar vṛdhe ṣaṣṭham avardhanta hy etarhi yajamānam evaitena vardhayanti
children.translated_text: Cattle are the <s>Iṣovṛdhīya</s>, for securing cattle. The fifth day is for nourishment, and the sixth is for increase. For at this point they have increased; by this they make the sacrificer himself increase.

children.text: krauñcaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Krauñca</s> is used.

children.text: kruṅṅ eṣyam ahar avindad eṣyam iva vai ṣaṣṭham ahar evaitena vindanti
children.translated_text: <s>Kruṅ</s> found the day that was to be sought. The sixth day is, as it were, to be sought; by this they find it.

children.text: vājadāvaryo bhavanti
children.translated_text: The <s>Vājadāvarī</s> verses are used.

children.text: annaṃ vai vājo 'nnādyasyāvaruddhyai yadā hi vā annam atha gaur athāśvo 'tha puruṣo vājī
children.translated_text: Food is <s>vāja</s>, for securing food and the eating of food. For when there is food, then the cow, then the horse, then the man is vigorous.

children.text: revatyo bhavanti pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Revatī</s> verses are used, for stability.

children.text: ṣaṇṇidhanī ṣaḍrātrasya dhṛtyai
children.translated_text: It has six <s>nidhana</s>s, for the support of the six-night rite.

children.text: āpo vai revatyas tā yat pṛṣṭhaṃ kuryur apaśur yajamānaḥ syāt paśūn asya nirdaheyur yatra vā āpo vivartante tad oṣadhayo jāyante 'tha yatrāvatiṣṭhante nirmṛtukās tatra bhavanti tasmāt pavamāne kurvanti parācā hi pavamānena stuvate
children.translated_text: The waters are the <s>Revatī</s> verses. If they were to make them the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, the sacrificer would be without cattle; they would burn away his cattle. Where waters turn aside, plants are born, but where they stand still, there they become seasonless. Therefore they make them in the <s>Pavamāna</s>, for they praise with the <s>Pavamāna</s> turned away.

children.text: methī vā iṣovṛdhīyaṃ rajjuḥ krauñcaṃ vatso vājadāvaryo revatyo mātaro yad etāny evaṃ sāmāni kriyanta evam eva prattāṃ dugdhe
children.translated_text: The <s>Iṣovṛdhīya</s> is the stake, the <s>Krauñca</s> is the rope, the <s>Vājadāvarī</s> verses are the calf, and the <s>Revatī</s> verses are the mothers. When these <s>sāman</s>s are performed in this way, he milks what has been given in just that way.

children.text: aukṣṇorandhre bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: The two <s>Aukṣṇorandhra</s>s are used.

children.text: ukṣṇorandhro vā etābhyāṃ kāvyo 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāllokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: With these two, <s>Ukṣṇorandhra Kāvya</s> saw the heavenly world directly, for the disclosure of the heavenly world. One who praises with them does not fall away from the heavenly world.

children.text: vājajid bhavati sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvaṃ vā ete vājaṃ jayanti ye ṣaṣṭham ahar āgacchanti
children.translated_text: The <s>Vājajit</s> is used, for attaining everything and for conquering everything. For those who come to the sixth day conquer all <s>vāja</s>.

children.text: annaṃ vai vājo 'nnādyasyāvaruddhyai
children.translated_text: Food is <s>vāja</s>, for securing food and the eating of food.

children.text: varuṇasāma bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Varuṇasāman</s> is used.

children.text: etena vai varuṇo rājyam ādhipatyam agacchad yaśo 'bhavad rājyam ādhipatyaṃ gacchati yaśo bhavati varuṇasāmnā tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: By this <s>Varuṇa</s> attained kingship and overlordship and became glorious. One who praises with the <s>Varuṇasāman</s> attains kingship and overlordship, and becomes glorious.

children.text: aṅgirasāṃ goṣṭho bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Goṣṭha</s> of the <s>Aṅgiras</s>es is used.

children.text: paśavo vai revatyo gauṣṭham eva tat paśubhyaḥ paryasyanti tam evainān pravartayanty avisraṃsāya
children.translated_text: The <s>Revatī</s> verses are cattle. Thereby they set a cow-stall around the cattle; they set them moving within it, so that they do not slip away.

children.text: ihavad vāmadevyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Vāmadevya</s> containing 'here' is used.

children.text: etena vai vāmadevo 'nnasya purodhām agacchad annaṃ vai brahmaṇaḥ purodhā annasyāvaruddhyai
children.translated_text: By this <s>Vāmadeva</s> attained the precedence of food. Food is the precedence of <s>brahman</s>, for securing food.

children.text: gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
children.translated_text: They praise on <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, for stability and for <s>brahmavarcasa</s>. With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up to it.

children.text: marutvatyo gāyatryo bhavanti tad u traiṣṭubhād rūpān na yanti stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Marutvatī</s> <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses are used; thereby they do not depart from the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> form. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: yātayāmāny anyāni chandāṃsy ayātayāmā gāyatrī tasmād gāyatrīṣu stuvanti
children.translated_text: The other metres are worn out; the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is unworn. Therefore they chant on <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses.

children.text: surūpa kṛtnum ūtaya ity abhyārambheṇa ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ tena ṣaṣṭham ahar ārabhante santatyai
children.translated_text: The verses beginning 'the fair-forming one, for help' are six-footed by way of commencement. This is the form of the sixth day; with it they commence the sixth day, for continuity.

children.text: ubhe yad indra rodasī iti ṣaṭpadāḥ ṣaṣṭhasyāhno rūpaṃ tena ṣaṣṭham ahar ārabhante santatyai
children.translated_text: The verses beginning 'When both heaven and earth, O <s>Indra</s>' are six-footed. This is the form of the sixth day; with it they commence the sixth day, for continuity.

children.text: revatīṣu vāravantīyaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Vāravantīya</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s> is used on the <s>Revatī</s> verses.

children.text: apāṃ vā eṣa raso yad revatyo revatīnāṃ raso yad vāravantīyaṃ sarasā eva tad revatīḥ prayuṅkte yad vāravantīyena pṛṣṭhena stuvate
children.translated_text: The <s>Revatī</s> verses are the sap of the waters, and the <s>Vāravantīya</s> is the sap of the <s>Revatī</s> verses. When they praise with the <s>Vāravantīya</s> <s>pṛṣṭha</s>, he thereby employs the <s>Revatī</s> verses with sap.

children.text: revad vā etad raivatyaṃ yad vāravantīyam asya revān revātyā jāyate
children.translated_text: This <s>Vāravantīya</s> is rich and <s>Raivatī</s> in character; from a rich woman a rich offspring is born for him.

children.text: revān bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows thus becomes rich.

children.text: keśine vā etad dālbhyāya sāmāvirabhavat tad enam abravīd agātāro mā gāyanti mā mayodgāsiṣur iti kathaṃ ta āgā bhagava ity abravīd āgeyam evāsmy āgāyann iva gāyet pratiṣṭhāyai tad alammaṃ pārijānataṃ paścādakṣaṃ śayānam etām āgāṃ gāyantam ajānāt tam abravīt puras tvā dadhā iti tam abruvan ko nv ayaṃ kasmā alam ity alaṃ nu vai mahyam iti tad alammasyālammatvam
children.translated_text: This <s>sāman</s> (chant) appeared to <s>Keśin Dālbhya</s>. It said to him, 'Let non-singers not sing me; let them not sing me aloud.' He said, 'How are you to be sung, venerable one?' It said, 'I am to be sung as an <s>āgā</s>; one should sing as though singing an <s>āgā</s>, for stability.' Then he recognized <s>Ālamma Pārijānata</s>, lying behind the axle, as singing this <s>āgā</s>. He said to him, 'I shall place you in front.' They said to him, 'Who now is this? For what is he fit?' 'He is quite fit for me,' he said. That is the <s>Ālamma</s>-nature of <s>Ālamma</s>.

children.text: iheheti gāyet pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: One should sing 'here, here,' for stability.

children.text: ṛṣabho raivato bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Raivata Ṛṣabha</s> is used.

children.text: paśavo vai raivatyaḥ paśuṣv eva tan mithunam apyarjati prajātyai na ha vā anṛṣabhāḥ paśavaḥ prajāyante
children.translated_text: The <s>Raivatī</s> verses are cattle; thereby he secures mating among cattle, for generation. For cattle without a bull do not reproduce.

children.text: śyeno bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Śyena</s> is used.

children.text: śyeno ha vai pūrvapretāni vayāṃsy āpnoti pūrvapretānīva vai pūrvāṇy ahāni teṣām āptyai śyenaḥ kriyate
children.translated_text: The falcon overtakes birds that have gone ahead. The preceding days are, as it were, those that have gone ahead; the <s>Śyena</s> is performed for overtaking them.

children.text: śyeno vā etad ahaḥ saṃpārayitum arhati sa hi vayasām āśiṣṭhas tasyānapahananāya sampāraṇāyaitat kriyate 'nto hi ṣaṣṭhaṃ cāhaḥ saptamaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The <s>Śyena</s> is able to carry this day across, for it is the swiftest of birds. This is done so that it is not struck down and so that it may be carried across, for the sixth day and the seventh day are an end-point.

children.text: brahmavādino vadanti yad bṛhad āyatanāni pṛṣṭhāny athaite dve gāyatryau dve jagatyau kva tarhi bṛhatyo bhavantīti
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahmavādin</s>s say, 'Since the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s have the <s>Bṛhat</s> as their base, while these are two <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses and two <s>Jagatī</s> verses, where then are the <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses?'

children.text: ye dve jagatyoḥ pade te gāyatryā upasaṃpadyete tat sarvā bṛhatyo bhavanty āyatane pṛṣṭhāni yātayatyāyatanavān bhavati
children.translated_text: The two feet that belong to the <s>Jagatī</s> verses are added to the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; thus they all become <s>Bṛhatī</s> verses. He sets the <s>pṛṣṭha</s>s in their base; he becomes possessed of a base.

children.text: ṣaṭpadāsu stuvanti ṣaḍrātrasya dhṛtyai
children.translated_text: They chant on six-footed verses, for the support of the six-night rite.

children.text: saptapadayā yajati saptamasyāhnaḥ santatyai stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He sacrifices with a seven-footed verse, for continuity with the seventh day. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: parisvāno giriṣṭhā iti parivatyo gāyatryo bhavanti sarvasya paryāptyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses beginning 'Roaring around, standing on the mountain' are <s>Parivatī</s> verses, for the encompassing of everything.

children.text: sasunveyo vasūnām iti paśavo vai vasu paśūnām avaruddhyai
children.translated_text: The verse beginning 'the one to be pressed among riches' is used. Cattle are wealth; it is for securing cattle.

children.text: taṃ vassakhāyo madāya iti vālakhilyāḥ
children.translated_text: The verses beginning 'Him, O friends, for exhilaration' are <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses.

children.text: vālakhilyāv etau tṛcau ṣaṣṭhe cāhani saptame ca
children.translated_text: These two triplets are <s>Vālakhilya</s> verses, on the sixth day and on the seventh.

children.text: yad etau vālakhilyau tṛcau bhavato 'hnor eva vyatiṣaṅgāyāvyatisraṃsāya santatyai
children.translated_text: When these two <s>Vālakhilya</s> triplets are used, it is for the interlinking of the two days, for their not slipping apart, and for continuity.

children.text: somāḥ pavanta indava ity anuṣṭubho nibhasado bhavanti pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> verses beginning 'The <s>Soma</s> drops flow' are <s>Nibhasad</s> verses, for stability.

children.text: ayā pavā pavasvainā vasūni iti triṣṭubhas satyo jagatyo rūpeṇa tasmājjagatīnāṃ loke kriyante
children.translated_text: The verses beginning 'Flow this way; flow yourself here to riches' are <s>Triṣṭubh</s> verses, but <s>Jagatī</s> by form; therefore they are performed in the place of the <s>Jagatī</s> verses.

children.text: gāyatraṃ bhavati yad eva gāyatrasya brāhmaṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatra</s> is used; whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> explanation of the <s>Gāyatra</s> applies.

children.text: vaidanvatāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaidanvata</s> chants are used.

children.text: vidanvān vai bhārgava indrasya pratyahaṃs taṃ śug ārchat sa tapo 'tapyata sa etāni vaidanvatāny apaśyat taiḥ śucam apāhatāpaśucaṃ hate vaidanvatais tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vidanvan Bhārgava</s> struck against <s>Indra</s>; anguish seized him. He performed austerity, and he saw these <s>Vaidanvata</s> chants. With them he drove away anguish. The one praising with the <s>Vaidanvata</s>s strikes away anguish.

children.text: bharadvājasya lomata bhavati
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s <s>Lomata</s> is used.

children.text: paśavo vai loma paśūnām avaruddhyai
children.translated_text: Hair is cattle; it is for securing cattle.

children.text: tad u dīrgham ity āhur āyur vai dīrgham āyuṣo 'varuddhyai
children.translated_text: And they say, 'That is long.' Life is long; it is for securing life.

children.text: kārṇaśravasaṃ bhavati śṛṇvanti tuṣṭuvānam
children.translated_text: The <s>Kārṇaśravasa</s> is used; people hear the one who praises.

children.text: karṇaśravā vā etad āṅgirasaḥ paśukāmaḥ sāmāpaśyat tena sahasraṃ paśūn asṛjata yad etat sāma bhavati paśūnāṃ puṣṭyai
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇaśravas Āṅgirasa</s>, desiring cattle, saw this <s>sāman</s>. With it he created a thousand cattle. When this <s>sāman</s> is used, it is for the thriving of cattle.

children.text: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaurīvita</s> is used; the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> explanation of the <s>Gaurīvita</s> applies.

children.text: madhuścyunnidhanaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: A <s>Madhuścyut</s>-<s>nidhana</s> is used.

children.text: paramasyānnādyasyāvaruddhyai paramaṃ vā etad annādyaṃ yan madhu
children.translated_text: It is for securing the highest food, for honey is the highest food.

children.text: prajāpater vā etau stanau yad ghṛtaścyunnidhanaṃ ca madhuścyunnidhanaṃ ca yajño vai prajāpatis tam etābhyāṃ dugdhe yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate taṃ dugdhe
children.translated_text: These two, the <s>Ghṛtaścyut</s>-<s>nidhana</s> and the <s>Madhuścyut</s>-<s>nidhana</s>, are the two breasts of <s>Prajāpati</s>. The sacrifice is <s>Prajāpati</s>; with these two he milks him. Whatever desire he desires, that he milks out.

children.text: krauñce bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: The two <s>Krauñca</s> chants are used.

children.text: śnauṣṭaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Śnauṣṭa</s> is used.

children.text: śnuṣṭir vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāt lokānna cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: With this, <s>Śnuṣṭi Āṅgirasa</s> saw the heavenly world directly. It is for the manifest vision of the heavenly world; the one praising with it does not fall from the heavenly world.

children.text: agner vā etad vaiśvānaraṃ sāma dīdihīti nidhanam upayanti dīdā eva hy agnir vaiśvānaraḥ
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>sāman</s> of <s>Agni</s>. They approach the <s>nidhana</s> 'shine forth,' for <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s> indeed shines.

children.text: nidhanāntāḥ pavamānā bhavanty ahno dhṛtyai stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pavamāna</s> chants have the <s>nidhana</s> as their ending, for the support of the day. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: brahmavādino vadanti prāyaṇato dvipadāḥ kāryā udayanatā3 iti
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahmavādin</s>s say, 'Should the two-footed verses be performed at the departure, or at the ascent?'

children.text: udayanata eva kāryāḥ puruṣo vai dvipadāḥ pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: They should be performed at the ascent itself. The two-footed verses are the person, for stability.

children.text: vācā vai sarvaṃ yajñaṃ tanvate tasmāt sarvāṃ vācaṃ puruṣo vadati sarvā hy asmin saṃstutā pratitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: By speech they extend the whole sacrifice; therefore a person speaks all speech, for all speech, when fully praised, becomes established in him.

children.text: gūrdo bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Gūrda</s> is used.

children.text: gopāyanānāṃ vai sattram āsīnānāṃ kirātakulyāv asuramāye antaḥparidhy asūn prākiratāṃ te agre tvan no antama ity agnim upāsīdaṃs tenāsūn aspṛṇvaṃs tad vāva te tarhy akāmayanta kāmasani sāma gūrdaḥ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
children.translated_text: When the <s>Gopāyana</s>s were sitting in a sacrificial session, the two <s>Kirātakulya</s>s, with Asura-magic, scattered their life-breaths inside the enclosing perimeter. At first they approached <s>Agni</s> with, 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are nearest to us.' By that they replenished their life-breaths. That indeed was what they desired then. The <s>Gūrda</s> is a desire-winning <s>sāman</s>; by it one secures desire itself.

children.text: gotamasya bhandra bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhandra</s> of <s>Gotama</s> is used.

children.text: āśiṣam evāsmā etenāśāste sāma hi satyāśīḥ
children.translated_text: With this he calls down a blessing for himself; for a <s>sāman</s> is truly a bringer of true blessing.

children.text: etena vai gotamo jemānaṃ mahimānam agacchat tasmād ye ca parāñco gotamād ye cārvāñcas ta ubhaye gotamā ṛṣayo bruvate
children.translated_text: By this, indeed, <s>Gotama</s> reached conquering greatness. Therefore both those who are earlier than <s>Gotama</s> and those who are later than him call themselves <s>Gotama</s> seers.

children.text: udvaṃśaputrā bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Udvaṃśaputrā</s> is used.

children.text: yad vā udvaṃśīyaṃ tad udvaṃśaputraḥ
children.translated_text: What belongs to <s>Udvaṃśa</s> is the <s>Udvaṃśaputra</s>.

children.text: ardheḍām atisvarati
children.translated_text: He sings beyond the <s>Ardheḍā</s>.

children.text: tasmād ūdhardhārā ati carantīḍāyām antataḥ paśuṣu pratitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Therefore the stream from the udder, passing beyond, finally comes to a firm place in the <s>iḍā</s> among cattle.

children.text: kﾱpta upariṣṭād ṛk sāma ca vimucyete abhy u svareṇa saptamam ahaḥ svarati santatyai
children.translated_text: After it has been arranged above, the verse and the <s>sāman</s> are released; with the upward chant he sings toward the seventh day, for continuity.

children.text: ūhuṣīva vā etarhi vāg yadā ṣaḍahaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate na bahu vaden nānyaṃ pṛcchen nānyasmai prabrūyāt
children.translated_text: At this point, when the <s>ṣaḍaha</s> is completed, speech is as though exhausted. He should not speak much, should not ask another, and should not declare anything to another.

children.text: madhu vāśayed ghṛtaṃ vā yathehuṣo bahaṃ pratyanakti tathā tat
children.translated_text: He should make it taste honey or ghee. As one anoints a beast that has carried a load, so is that.

children.text: trayastriṃśa eva stomo bhavati pratiṣṭhāyai devatāsu vā eṣa pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stoma</s> is precisely the thirty-threefold one, for stability; for this one is established among the deities.

children.text: Chapter 14
āpyante vā etat stomāś chandāṃsi yat ṣaḍaha āpyate
children.translated_text: When the <s>ṣaḍaha</s> is completed, the <s>stoma</s>s and metres are thereby filled out.

children.text: āpte ṣaḍahe chandāṃsi stomān kṛtvā prayanti
children.translated_text: When the <s>ṣaḍaha</s> has been completed, they set out after making the metres into <s>stoma</s>s.

children.text: pra kāvyam uśanevara bruvāṇa iti gāyatryā rūpeṇa prayanti
children.translated_text: They set out in the form of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, with the verse, 'Proclaiming inspired wisdom like <s>Uśanas</s>.'

children.text: iyaṃ vai gāyatry asyām eva pratiṣṭhāya prayanti
children.translated_text: This earth is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; having taken their stand on this very earth, they set out.

children.text: triṣṭup pratipad bhavati
children.translated_text: The opening verse is in <s>Triṣṭubh</s> metre.

children.text: ojo vīryaṃ triṣṭubojasyeva vīrye parākramya prayanti
children.translated_text: The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is strength and heroic power; having advanced in strength and heroic power itself, they set out.

children.text: stotrīyas tṛco bhavati prāṇāpānānām avaruddhyai
children.translated_text: The <s>stotrīya</s> triplet is used, for securing the out-breath and in-breath.

children.text: harivatyo bhavanti chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
children.translated_text: The verses containing 'hari' are used, so that the <s>chandoma</s>s may not become stale or exhausted.

children.text: dvādaśarcau bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: There are two sets of twelve verses.

children.text: dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaram eva tatpūrvasmai ṣaḍahāya pratyudyacchati savīvadhatāyai
children.translated_text: Twelve months are a year; thereby he raises up the year for the preceding <s>ṣaḍaha</s>, so that it may have its proper support.

children.text: caturviṃśatir bhavanti caturviṃśatir ardhamāsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaram eva tatpūrvasmai ṣaḍahāya pratyudyacchati savīvadhatāyai
children.translated_text: There are twenty-four; twenty-four half-months are a year. Thereby he raises up the year for the preceding <s>ṣaḍaha</s>, so that it may have its proper support.

children.text: dṛta aindrota iti hovācābhipratārī kākṣasenir ye mahāvṛkṣasyāgraṃ gacchanti ka te tato bhavanti pra rājan pakṣiṇaḥ patanty avāpakṣāḥ padyante
children.translated_text: '<s>Dṛta Aindrota</s>,' said <s>Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni</s>, 'when people go to the top of a great tree, what becomes of them from there?' 'Winged birds fly forth, O king; those without wings fall down.'

children.text: ye vai vidvāṃsas te pakṣiṇo ye 'vidvāṃsas te 'pakṣās trivṛt pañcadaśāv eva stomau pakṣau kṛtvā svargaṃ lokaṃ prayanti
children.translated_text: Those who know are the winged ones; those who do not know are wingless. Making the <s>Trivṛt</s> and <s>Pañcadaśa</s> <s>stoma</s>s into their two wings, they set out for the heavenly world.

children.text: caturviṃśa eva stomo bhavati tejase brahmavarcasāya ||
children.translated_text: The <s>stoma</s> is precisely the twenty-fourfold one, for radiance and <s>brahmavarcasa</s> (sacred brilliance).

children.text: mūrdhānaṃ divo aratim pṛthivyā ity āgneyam ājyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Āgneya Ājya</s> is the verse, 'The head of heaven, the active one of earth.'

children.text: mūrdhā vā eṣa divo yas tṛtīyas trirātraḥ
children.translated_text: For this third <s>trirātra</s> is the head of heaven.

children.text: vaiśvānaram ṛta ājātam agnim iti vaiśvānara iti vā agneḥ priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainaṃ tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
children.translated_text: The verse is, '<s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Agni</s>, born from truth.' <s>Vaiśvānara</s> is <s>Agni</s>'s dear abode; by that dear abode he approaches him indirectly.

children.text: pra vo mitrāya gāyata iti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ maitrāvaruṇaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī vai mitrāvaruṇayoḥ priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainau tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
children.translated_text: The verse, 'Sing forth for <s>Mitra</s>,' is the <s>Maitrāvaruṇa</s> addressed to Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth are the dear abode of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>; by that dear abode he approaches the two of them indirectly.

children.text: indrāyāhi citrabhānav ity ārbhavam aindram ṛbhavo vā indrasya priyaṃ dhāma priyeṇaivainaṃ tad dhāmnā parokṣam upaśikṣati
children.translated_text: The verse, 'Come to <s>Indra</s>, O bright-shining one,' is the <s>Aindra</s> connected with the <s>Ṛbhu</s>s. The <s>Ṛbhu</s>s are <s>Indra</s>'s dear abode; by that dear abode he approaches him indirectly.

children.text: tam īḍiṣva yo arciṣā ity aniruktam aindrāgnaṃ devatānām anabhidharṣāyottamārdhe 'nirāha devatānām apraṇāśāya stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The verse, 'Praise him who with his flame,' is an unexpressed <s>Aindrāgna</s>, for the deities' inviolability. In the latter half he leaves it unspoken, so that the deities may not be lost. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: vṛṣā pavasva dhāraya iti gāyatrī bhavatyahno dhṛtyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verse, 'Flow, a bull, with a stream,' is used, for the support of the day.

children.text: vṛṣaṇvatyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa traiṣṭubhaṃ hyetad ahaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Triṣṭubh</s>s containing the word 'bull' are used in the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, for this day is <s>Traiṣṭubha</s>.

children.text: punānaḥ soma dhāraya iti dhṛtyai
children.translated_text: The verse, 'Purifying yourself, O <s>Soma</s>, with a stream,' is used for support.

children.text: pro ayāsīd indur indrasya niṣkṛtam iti pravatyo bhavanti praṇinīṣeṇyam iva hyetad ahaḥ
children.translated_text: The forward-moving verses are used, with, 'The bright drop has gone forth to <s>Indra</s>'s prepared place,' for this day is as though to be led onward.

children.text: jagatyaḥ satyas triṣṭubho rūpeṇa tasmāt triṣṭubhāṃ loke kriyante
children.translated_text: Though they are <s>Jagatī</s> verses, they have the form of <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; therefore they are performed in the place of the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>s.

children.text: santani bhavati saptamasyāhnaḥ santatyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Santani</s> is used, for the continuity of the seventh day.

children.text: yathā vai vyokasau vipradravata evam ete ṣaṣṭhaṃ cāhaḥ saptamaṃ ca vipradravatas tau yathā samānīya saṃyujyād evam evaite etena sāmnā saṃyunakti
children.translated_text: Just as two people living in separate houses run apart, so these two, the sixth day and the seventh day, run apart. As one would bring those two together and join them, so he joins these two with this <s>sāman</s>.

children.text: yajño vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat sa suparṇarūpaṃ kṛtvācarat taṃ devā etaiḥ sāmabhirārabhanta yajña iva vā eṣa yacchandomā yajñasyaivaiṣa ārambhaḥ
children.translated_text: The sacrifice withdrew from the gods; taking the form of <s>Suparṇa</s>, it went about. The gods took hold of it with these <s>sāman</s>s. What are called the <s>chandoma</s>s are, as it were, the sacrifice; this is the taking hold of the sacrifice itself.

children.text: rohitakūlīyaṃ bhavaty ājijityāyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Rohitakūlīya</s> is used, for victory in the race.

children.text: etena vai viśvāmitro rohitābhyāṃ rohitakūla ājim ajayat
children.translated_text: By this, indeed, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> won the race at <s>Rohitakūla</s> with the two red steeds.

children.text: viśvāmitro bharatānāṃ manassatyāyāt so 'dantibhir nāma janatayāṃśaṃ prāsyate māṃ māṃ yūyaṃ astikāṃ jayāthemāni mahyaṃ yūyaṃ pūrayātha yadīmāvidaṃ rohitāvaśmācitaṃ kūlam udvahāta iti sa ete sāmanī apaśyat tābhyāṃ yuktvā prāsedhat sa udajayat
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, true in thought among the <s>Bharata</s>s, went forth. Among a people called the <s>Adantibhi</s>s, a share was offered to him: 'Win me, win me; fill these things for me, if these two red ones carry up this stone-built bank.' He saw these two <s>sāman</s>s; having yoked with them, he drove forward, and he won.

children.text: ājir vā eṣa pratato yad dvādaśāhas tasyaite ujjityai
children.translated_text: This extended <s>dvādaśāha</s> is a race; these two are for winning it.

children.text: kaṇvarathantaraṃ bhavati tejo vā etad rathantarasya yat kaṇvarathantaram
children.translated_text: The <s>Kaṇvarathantara</s> is used. The <s>Kaṇvarathantara</s> is the radiance of the <s>Rathantara</s>.

children.text: sarasam eva tad rathantaraṃ prayuṅkte yat kaṇvarathantareṇa saptame 'hani stuvate
children.translated_text: That <s>Rathantara</s> he employs as full of sap, in that they praise on the seventh day with the <s>Kaṇvarathantara</s>.

children.text: jāmi dvādaśāhasyāstīti ha smāhogradevo rājanir bārhataṃ ṣaṣṭham ahar bārhataṃ saptamaṃ yat kaṇvarathantaraṃ bhavati tenājāmi
children.translated_text: <s>Ugradeva Rājani</s> used to say, "There is sameness in the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>." The sixth day is <s>Bārhata</s>, and the seventh is <s>Bārhata</s>; because the <s>Kaṇvarathantara</s> is used, by that it is without sameness.

children.text: gauṅgavaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Gauṅgava</s> is used.

children.text: agnir akāmayatānnādaḥ syām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa etad gauṅgavam apaśyat tenānnādo 'bhavad yad annaṃ vitvā gardadyad agaṅgūyat tad gauṅgavasya gauṅgavatvam annādyasyāvaruddhyai gauṅgavaṃ kiyate
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> desired, "May I be an eater of food." He practiced austerity. He saw this <s>Gauṅgava</s>; by it he became an eater of food. When, having found food, he roared and made the sound gaṅgū, that is the <s>Gauṅgava</s>'s being <s>Gauṅgava</s>. The <s>Gauṅgava</s> is performed for securing food-eating.

children.text: yat sāma devatā praśaṃyati tena yajamānāḥ satyāśiṣaḥ satyāśiṣo 'sāmeti vai sattram āsate satyāśiṣa eva bhavanti
children.translated_text: Because a <s>sāman</s> praises a deity, through it the sacrificers have true blessings. They sit in the <s>sattra</s> saying, "May we have true blessings"; they become precisely those whose blessings are true.

children.text: āyāsyaṃ bhavati tiraścīnanidhanaṃ pratiṣṭhāyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Āyāsya</s> is used, with a transverse <s>nidhana</s>, for stability.

children.text: ayāsyo vā āṅgirasa ādityānāṃ dīkṣitānām annam āśnāt sa vyabhraṃśata sa etāny āyāsyāny apaśyat tair ātmānaṃ samaśrīṇād vibhraṣṭam iva vai saptamam ahar yad etat sāma bhavaty ahar eva tena saṃśrīṇāti
children.translated_text: <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s> ate the food of the consecrated <s>Āditya</s>s. He fell away. He saw these <s>Āyāsya</s>s; with them he restored himself after he had fallen away. The seventh day is, as it were, fallen away. When this <s>sāman</s> is used, with it he restores the day itself.

children.text: pravadbhargavaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pravadbhargava</s> is used.

children.text: vayaṃ ghatvā sutāvanta iti bṛhatyo varṣīyaśchanda ākramate 'napabhraṃśāya
children.translated_text: The verses beginning "Vayaṃ ghatvā sutāvantaḥ" are <s>Bṛhatī</s>s. He steps onto a more ample metre, so that there may be no slipping down.

children.text: nakiṣṭaṃ karmaṇā naśad iti bṛhatyaḥ satyo 'bhyārambheṇa jagatyaḥ
children.translated_text: The verses beginning "Nakiṣṭaṃ karmaṇā naśat," though <s>Bṛhatī</s>s, are <s>Jagatī</s>s by means of an added opening.

children.text: apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yajjyāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etā abhyārambheṇa jagatyo bhavanty ahna eva pratyuttambhāya
children.translated_text: This is like a slipping down, when they pass from a larger <s>stoma</s> to a smaller <s>stoma</s>. Since these become <s>Jagatī</s>s by means of an added opening, it is for propping up the day itself.

children.text: abhinidhanaṃ kāṇvaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Abhinidhana Kāṇva</s> is used.

children.text: abhinidhanena vā indro vṛtrāya vajraṃ prāharat tam astṛṇuta stṛṇute bhrātṛvyam abhinidhanena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: With the <s>Abhinidhana</s>, <s>Indra</s> hurled the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) at <s>Vṛtra</s> and struck him down. One who praises with the <s>Abhinidhana</s> strikes down his rival.

children.text: vaikhānasā vā ṛṣaya indrasya priyā āsaṃs tān rahasyur devamalimluḍ munimaraṇe 'mārayat taṃ devā abruvan kva tarṣayo 'bhūvānn iti tān praiṣam aicchat tān nāvindat sa imān lokān ekadhāreṇāpunāt tān munimaraṇe 'vindat tān etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vaikhānasaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> seers were dear to <s>Indra</s>. <s>Rahasyu Devamalimluḍ</s> killed them at <s>Munimaraṇa</s>. The gods said to him, "Where have the seers gone?" He sought a summons for them, but did not find them. He purified these worlds with a single stream and found them at <s>Munimaraṇa</s>. With this <s>sāman</s> he set them in motion again. That indeed was what he desired then. The <s>Vaikhānasa</s> is a desire-winning <s>sāman</s>; by it he secures desire itself. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: yas te mado vareṇya iti gāyatrī bhavati madavad vai rasavat tṛtīyasavanaṃ madam eva tad rasaṃ dadhāti
children.translated_text: The <s>Gāyatrī</s> verse beginning "Yas te mado vareṇyaḥ" is used. The third pressing is indeed full of exhilaration and sap; thereby he places exhilaration and sap in it.

children.text: eṣasya dhārayā suta iti kakubhaḥ satyo 'bhyārambheṇa triṣṭubhaḥ
children.translated_text: The verses beginning "Eṣasya dhārayā sutaḥ," though <s>Kakubh</s>s, are <s>Triṣṭubh</s>s by means of an added opening.

children.text: apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yat jyāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etā abhyārambheṇa triṣṭubho bhavanty ahna eva pratyuttambhāya
children.translated_text: This is like a slipping down, when they pass from a larger <s>stoma</s> to a smaller <s>stoma</s>. Since these become <s>Triṣṭubh</s>s by means of an added opening, it is for propping up the day itself.

children.text: sakhāya āniṣīdata iti vālakhilyā vālakhilyāv etau tṛcau ṣaṣṭhe cāhani saptame ca yad etau vālakhilyau tṛcau bhavato 'hnor eva vyatiṣaṅgāyāvyavasraṃsāya santatyai
children.translated_text: The verses beginning "Sakhāya ā niṣīdata" are <s>Vālakhilya</s>s. These two triplets are <s>Vālakhilya</s>s, on the sixth day and on the seventh. Since these two <s>Vālakhilya</s> triplets occur, it is for the interweaving of the days themselves, for their not slipping apart, and for continuity.

children.text: purojitī vo andhasa iti virāḍ annaṃ virāḍ annādyasyāvaruddhyai
children.translated_text: The verse beginning "Purojitī vo andhasaḥ" is a <s>Virāj</s>. The <s>Virāj</s> is food; it is for securing food-eating.

children.text: pra vājy akṣār ity akṣarapaṅktiḥ stomānāṃ prabhūtiḥ
children.translated_text: The verse beginning "Pra vājī akṣār" is an <s>Akṣarapaṅkti</s>; it is the source of the <s>stoma</s>s.

children.text: atho etaddhyevaitarhi chando 'yātayāma yad akṣarapaṅktis tena chandomā ayātayāmānaḥ kriyante
children.translated_text: Moreover, this metre at this point is indeed unexhausted, namely the <s>Akṣarapaṅkti</s>. Through it the <s>Chandoma</s>s are made unexhausted.

children.text: brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā ityetacchandaso yad etā akṣarapaṅktaya iti brūyāt
children.translated_text: The expounders of <s>brahman</s> say, "Since in the <s>Ṣaḍaha</s> the <s>stoma</s>s and metres are attained, what metres do the <s>Chandoma</s>s have?" One should say, "These <s>Akṣarapaṅkti</s>s are those metres."

children.text: ye somāsaḥ parāvati iti parāvatam iva vā etarhi yajño gatas tam evaitenānvicchanti
children.translated_text: The verse beginning "Ye somāsaḥ parāvati" is used. At this point the sacrifice has gone, as it were, to a distant place; with this they seek it out.

children.text: dakṣaṇidhanaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Dakṣa-nidhana</s> is used.

children.text: prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tā asmāt sṛṣṭā abalā ivācchādayaṃstāsv etena sāmnā dakṣāyety ojo vīryam adadhād yad etat sāma bhavaty oja eva vīryam ātman dhatte
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> created creatures. Once created, they were like feeble beings and hid from him. Into them, with this <s>sāman</s>, saying "for skill and strength," he placed might and heroic power. When this <s>sāman</s> is used, he places might and heroic power in himself.

children.text: śārkaraṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Śārkara</s> is used.

children.text: indraṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny astuvan sa śarkaraṃ śiśumārarṣim upetyābravīt stuhi meti so 'paḥ praskandann abravīd etāvato 'haṃ tvāṃ stuyām iti tasmād apāṃ vegam avejayat sa hīna ivāmanyata sa etat sāmāpaśyat tenāpo 'nusamāśnuta tad vāva sa tarhyakāmayata kāmasani sāma śārkaraṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
children.translated_text: All beings praised <s>Indra</s>. He approached <s>Śarkara Śiśumāra Ṛṣi</s> and said, "Praise me." Leaping into the waters, he said, "Only to this extent shall I praise you." From that he shook off the force of the waters. He thought himself, as it were, deficient. He saw this <s>sāman</s>; with it he fully gained the waters. That indeed was what he desired then. The <s>Śārkara</s> is a desire-winning <s>sāman</s>; by it he secures desire itself.

children.text: plavo bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Plava</s> is used.

children.text: samudraṃ vā ete prasnāntīty āhur ye dvādaśāham upayantīti yo vā aplavaḥ samudraṃ prarunāti na sa tata udeti yataḥ plavo bhavati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai
children.translated_text: They say, "Those who undertake the <s>Dvādaśāha</s> plunge into the ocean." One who enters the ocean without a raft does not rise up from it. Therefore the <s>Plava</s> is used, for complete attainment of the heavenly world.

children.text: ativiśvāni duritā taremeti yad evaiṣāṃ duṣṭutaṃ duśśastaṃ tad etena taranti
children.translated_text: The verse says, "May we cross beyond all difficulties." Whatever among them is badly praised or badly recited, by this they cross over it.

children.text: ekādaśākṣaraṇidhano bhavaty ekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub ojīvīryaṃ triṣṭub ojasy eva vīrye pratitiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: It has a <s>nidhana</s> of eleven syllables. The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> has eleven syllables; the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> is might and heroic power. He becomes established in might itself, in heroic power.

children.text: gaurīvitaṃ bhavati yad eva gaurīvitasya brāhmaṇam
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaurīvita</s> is used; whatever is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> explanation of the <s>Gaurīvita</s> applies.

children.text: kārtayaśaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Kārtayaśa</s> is used.

children.text: hīti nidhanam upayanti pāpmano 'pahatyai
children.translated_text: They employ the <s>nidhana</s> "hī," for driving away evil.

children.text: apa pāpmānaṃ hate kārtayaśena tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: One who praises with the <s>Kārtayaśa</s> drives evil away.

children.text: sauhaviṣaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Sauhaviṣa</s> is used.

children.text: suhavir vā etenāṅgiraso 'ñjasā svargaṃ lokam apaśyat svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai svargāllokān na cyavate tuṣṭuvānaḥ
children.translated_text: By this, <s>Suhavis Āṅgirasa</s> directly saw the heavenly world. It is for the proclamation of the heavenly world; the one who praises with it does not fall away from the heavenly world.

children.text: brahmavādino vadanti yat ṣaḍahe stomāś chandāṃsy āpyante kiṃ chandasaś chandomā iti puruṣaś chandasa iti brūyāt puruṣo vai pāṅktaḥ puruṣo dvipadā chandomānām ayātayāmatāyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahmavādin</s>s say, 'When in the six-day rite the <s>stoma</s>s are made complete with the metres, what, in respect of metre, are the <s>Chandoma</s>s?' One should say, 'The person is the metre.' The person is indeed <s>pāṅkta</s> (fivefold), and the person is represented by two-footed verses, for the unworn character of the <s>Chandoma</s>s.

children.text: jarābodhīyaṃ bhavaty annādyasyāvaruddhyai
children.translated_text: The <s>Jarābodhīya</s> is used, for securing food and the eating of food.

children.text: annaṃ vai jarābodhīyaṃ mukhaṃ gāyatrī mukha eva tad annaṃ dhatte 'nnam atti
children.translated_text: The <s>Jarābodhīya</s> is food, and the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the mouth. Thus he places food in the mouth; he eats food.

children.text: annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda
children.translated_text: He who knows thus becomes an eater of food.

children.text: gāyatrīṣu stuvanti pratiṣṭhāyai brahmavarcasāya yenaiva prāṇena prayanti tam abhyudyanti
children.translated_text: They praise on <s>Gāyatrī</s> verses, for stability and for <s>brahmavarcasa</s>. With the very breath by which they set forth, they rise up to it.

children.text: iḍāntāḥ pāvamānā bhavanti paśavo vā iḍāḥ paśavaś chandomāḥ paśuṣv eva tat paśūn dadhāti stomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pavamāna</s> chants have <s>Iḍā</s> as their ending. The <s>Iḍā</s>s are cattle; the <s>Chandoma</s>s are cattle. Thus he places cattle among cattle. It is the <s>stoma</s>.

children.text: ā te vatso mano yamad ity apacchid iva vā etad yajñakāṇḍaṃ yad ukthāni yad eti salomatvāyaiva
children.translated_text: The verse beginning 'May your calf restrain the mind' is used. This section of the sacrifice, namely the <s>uktha</s>s, is as though cut off; when this verse comes in, it is precisely so that it may have hair.

children.text: tvaṃ na indrābhara iti pūrṇāḥ kakubhaḥ
children.translated_text: The full <s>Kakubh</s> verses begin 'You, O <s>Indra</s>, bring to us.'

children.text: apabhraṃśa iva vā eṣa yajjyāyasaḥ stomāt kanīyāṃsaṃ stomam upayanti yad etāḥ pūrṇāḥ kakubho bhavanty anapabhraṃśāya
children.translated_text: It is a kind of falling away when they pass from a greater <s>stoma</s> to a smaller <s>stoma</s>. Since these are full <s>Kakubh</s> verses, it is so that there may be no falling away.

children.text: vatsaś ca vai medhātithiś ca kāṇvāv āstāṃ taṃ vatsaṃ medhātithir ākrośad abrāhmaṇo 'si śūdrāputra iti so 'bravīd ṛtenāgniṃ vyayāva yataro nau brahmīyān iti vātsena vatso vyain maidhātithena medhātithis tasya na loma ca nauṣat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma vātsaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
children.translated_text: <s>Vatsa</s> and <s>Medhātithi</s> were both <s>Kāṇva</s>s. <s>Medhātithi</s> reviled <s>Vatsa</s>, saying, 'You are no Brahmin; you are the son of a Śūdra woman.' He said, 'Let us pass through fire by truth, whichever of us is more possessed of <s>brahman</s>.' <s>Vatsa</s> passed through with the <s>Vātsa</s>, and <s>Medhātithi</s> with the <s>Maidhātitha</s>; not even a hair of him was singed. That indeed was what he then desired. The <s>Vātsa</s> is a desire-winning <s>sāman</s>; by it one secures desire.

children.text: sauśravasaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Sauśravasa</s> is used.

children.text: upagur vai sauśravasaḥ kutsasyauravasya purohita āsīt sa kutsaḥ paryaśapad ya indraṃ yajātā iti sa indraḥ suśravasam upetyābravīd yajasva māśanāyāmivā iti tam ayajata sa indraḥ puroḍāśas taḥ kutsam upetyābravīd ayakṣata mā kva te pariśaptam abhūd iti kas tvā yaṣṭeti suśravā iti sa kutsa aurava upāgāḥ sauśravasasyodgāyata audumbaryā śiro 'chinat sa suśravā indram abravīt tvattanād vai medam īdṛg upāgād iti tam etena sāmnā samairayat tad vāva sa tarhy akāmayata kāmasani sāma sauśravasaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
children.translated_text: <s>Upagu Sauśravasa</s> was the household priest of <s>Kutsa Aurava</s>. <s>Kutsa</s> pronounced a curse: 'Whoever should sacrifice to <s>Indra</s>...' Then <s>Indra</s> approached <s>Suśravas</s> and said, 'Sacrifice to me; I am as though hungry.' He sacrificed to him. <s>Indra</s>, with the sacrificial cake, went to <s>Kutsa</s> and said, 'He has sacrificed to me. What has become of your curse?' 'Who sacrificed to you?' he asked. '<s>Suśravas</s>,' he said. Then <s>Kutsa Aurava</s> went up while the <s>Sauśravasa</s> was being sung and cut off his head with a fig-wood implement. <s>Suśravas</s> said to <s>Indra</s>, 'This has come upon me in such a way because of you.' With this <s>sāman</s> he restored him. That indeed was what he then desired. The <s>Sauśravasa</s> is a desire-winning <s>sāman</s>; by it one secures desire.

children.text: vīṅkaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The <s>Vīṅka</s> is used.

children.text: cyavano vai dādhīco 'śvinoḥ priya āsīt so 'jīryat tam etena sāmnāpsu vyaiṅkayatāṃ taṃ punaryuvānam akurutāṃ tad vāva tau tarhy akāmayetāṃ kāmasani sāma vīṅkaṃ kāmam evaitenāvarundhe
